title: Acyclicity of the annihilator of an integer in an injective module sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $\Lambda$ any commutative ring. Let $J$ be an injective object in the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\acute et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For $n>0$ put $E=\ker(n\operatorname{id}_J)$, a genuine kernel in this abelian category. The underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] satisfies $H^q(X,E)=0$ for every $q>0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. This is on X itself and asserts no restriction acyclicity.

source.place: Tag 03FD, proof, and Tag 03FC; quotient-ring restriction/coextension adjunction

proof.text: Put r=(n : Λ), R=Λ/(r), and K=coextendScalars(Λ→R)(I). Use the existing Sheaf.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj: restriction of scalars preserves monomorphisms and hence its right adjoint sends the injective I to an injective R-module sheaf K. No regularity of r is needed.

Construct the short complex with first object Res(K), counit f, and second map r id_I, using the zero-composite proof of the existing ModuleCat.coextendQuotientShortComplex sectionwise. ModuleCat.exact_coextendQuotientShortComplex and mono_coextendQuotientShortComplex_f apply sectionwise without any nonzerodivisor hypothesis. Evaluation detects presheaf homology, so the presheaf sequence is exact and f is monic. Exact sheafification transports exactness back to sheaves. ShortComplex.Exact.fIsKernel then identifies Res(K) with kernel(r id_I) by uniqueness of kernels.

Apply the proved subsingleton_H_underlying_of_injective_module to the injective R-module sheaf K. Its underlying abelian sheaf is definitionally the one underlying Res(K). Transport the resulting subsingleton through the kernel isomorphism, the coefficient-forgetful functor, and functorH. Finally Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul identifies r id_I with n • id_I. This works also for n=0, though the unchanged public statement requires n>0; n=1, zero rings and empty schemes are included.
